mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when GDPC1 falls by more than 0.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and depresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction relative to its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening in an inflationary environment, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal income (PAYEMS) over the prior six months signals robust household demand, which boosts consumption-sensitive sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, PAYEMS) > 0.7 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when the correlation between HOUST and PAYEMS exceeds 0.7 over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market recovery, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows above 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months in a post-recession environment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which reduces earnings across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of aggressive monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-mo MA for 6 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS not < 1% (monetary easing)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month MA for six months and monetary policy is not easing (FEDFUNDS not < 1%).
